# Judges Chapter 21 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), c. 1008 CE | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JDG_page_291.jpg, JDG_page_292.jpg

1. And the men of Yisrael had sworn at Mitspah, saying, "Not one of us shall give his daughter to Binyamin as a wife."

2. And the people came to Beit-El and sat there until the evening before God. And they lifted their voices and wept a great weeping.

3. And they said, "Why, O YHWH, God of Yisrael, has this happened in Yisrael, that today one tribe should be missing from Yisrael?"

4. And it was on the next day, and the people rose early and built there an altar and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings.

5. And the sons of Yisrael said, "Who [is there] among all the tribes of Yisrael who did not come up in the assembly to YHWH?" For the great oath had been [taken] concerning anyone who did not come up to YHWH at Mitspah, saying, "He shall surely be put to death."

6. And the sons of Yisrael had compassion for Binyamin their brother, and they said, "Today one tribe has been cut off from Yisrael.

7. "What shall we do for them — for those who remain — for wives, since we have sworn by YHWH not to give them [any] of our daughters as wives?"

8. And they said, "Which one [is there] of the tribes of Yisrael that did not come up to YHWH at Mitspah?" And behold, no one had come to the camp from Yavesh-Gil'ad, to the assembly.

9. And the people were mustered, and behold, there was no one there of the inhabitants of Yavesh-Gil'ad.

10. And the congregation sent there twelve thousand men of the sons of valor and commanded them, saying, "Go and strike the inhabitants of Yavesh-Gil'ad with the edge of the sword — and the women and the little ones.

11. "And this [is] the thing that you shall do: every male and every woman who has known the lying with a male you shall devote to destruction."

12. And they found among the inhabitants of Yavesh-Gil'ad four hundred young women, virgins, who had not known a man by the lying with a male. And they brought them to the camp at Shiloh, which [is] in the land of K'na'an.

13. And the whole congregation sent and spoke to the sons of Binyamin who [were] at the rock of Rimmon and proclaimed peace to them.

14. And Binyamin returned at that time, and they gave them the women whom they had kept alive from the women of Yavesh-Gil'ad. But they did not find enough for them.

15. And the people had compassion for Binyamin, for YHWH had made a breach in the tribes of Yisrael.

16. And the elders of the congregation said, "What shall we do for those who remain for wives, since women have been destroyed from Binyamin?"

17. And they said, "[There must be] an inheritance for the survivors of Binyamin, and a tribe shall not be blotted out from Yisrael.

18. "And we are not able to give them wives from our daughters." For the sons of Yisrael had sworn, saying, "Cursed [be] the one giving a wife to Binyamin."

19. And they said, "Behold, [there is] a feast of YHWH in Shiloh from year to year, which [is] north of Beit-El, on the east side of the highway that goes up from Beit-El to Sh'khem, and south of L'vonah."

20. And they commanded the sons of Binyamin, saying, "Go and lie in ambush in the vineyards.

21. "And see — and behold, if the daughters of Shiloh come out to dance in the dances, then come out from the vineyards and seize for yourselves each man his wife from the daughters of Shiloh, and go to the land of Binyamin.

22. "And it shall be, when their fathers or their brothers come to contend with us, that we will say to them, 'Be gracious to them for our sake, for we did not take for each man his wife in battle, nor did you give [them] to them, so you would now be guilty.'"

23. And the sons of Binyamin did so and took wives according to their number, from the dancers whom they seized. And they went and returned to their inheritance and built the cities and dwelt in them.

24. And the sons of Yisrael went from there at that time, each man to his tribe and to his clan, and they went out from there each man to his inheritance.

25. In those days there was no king in Yisrael. Each man did the right in his own eyes.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **v.5 — "the great oath" (hashvu'ah hag'dolah):** The oath not to give daughters to Benjamin in marriage creates a catch-22: having nearly destroyed a tribe, they now have no legal way to preserve it. The oath was itself rash — echoing Jephthah's rash vow (11:30-31).

2. **v.10-12 — The destruction of Jabesh-Gilead:** To solve the oath-problem, they destroy an Israelite city that failed to attend the assembly. The solution to one atrocity is another atrocity. The language echoes the cherem of chapter 20 — the cycle of violence is self-perpetuating.

3. **v.19-23 — The abduction at Shiloh:** The legal fiction is elaborate: the Benjaminites are told to "seize" (chataf) wives from the dancing women. If the fathers protest, the elders will argue that technically no one "gave" their daughters — so the oath is not violated. This is the book's final moral commentary: law has become a tool for justifying violence.

4. **v.25 — "each man did the right in his own eyes":** ish hayyashar b'einav ya'aseh — the full refrain, identical to 17:6. This is the book's last word. The four occurrences (17:6; 18:1; 19:1; 21:25) frame the appendix, and this final statement encompasses the entire book. The word yashar ("right/straight") is the cruel irony: moral chaos wearing the mask of righteousness.

— EMET, AI Translator
